title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure in an automated licence-plate reader, and it propagated into a physical confrontation. The camera matched a plate to a stolen-vehicle record, but the image it captured was of a different vehicle than the one flagged. The error was not caught before officers acted on it, so the alert arrived as an unverified claim of a stolen truck and was treated as grounds for a felony stop.

The failure sits at the handoff between an automated alert and a human decision to use force. Nothing in the reporting shows a step where the plate read was confirmed against the vehicle in front of the officers before they drew weapons and deployed a dog. Catching it would have required that confirmation, or a system that flags low-confidence reads rather than issuing them as stolen-vehicle hits.

What is not established is why the camera misread the plate, whether the department's investigation into the officers has concluded, and whether the dropped charges reflect a finding about the stop itself. The department's own review found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and that finding is a departmental conclusion, not an adjudication of the alert's accuracy.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police stopped a red Dodge Ram after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged its plate as stolen. The camera image actually matched a Chevy Malibu, not the truck. Officers approached with guns drawn and ordered driver Brandon Upchurch out. Body cam video shows him exiting with his hands up before walking onto the grass, where a K-9 handler released the dog. Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. Officers later confirmed the plate was not stolen and that the alert was a misread. He received medical attention at the scene.

Police said they believed Upchurch might flee and did not know if he or his passenger had weapons. Department policy requires handlers to weigh the crime's severity, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or hiding before deploying a dog. Multiple officers are under investigation, and body cam footage was released Monday.
